body:
## Problem

Class: masked-failure (a gate-shaped check that does not run the checks it
appears to gate).

`lint.yml` invokes `make lint-fish`, `make lint-markdown`, `make lint-json`
individually instead of `make lint`, and never invokes `make test-unit` or
`make test-integration`. Two lint targets and the entire test suite are
unreachable from CI.

## Evidence

`Makefile:64`:

    lint: lint-fish lint-markdown lint-md-tables lint-json lint-editorconfig

`.github/workflows/lint.yml:41-51` runs only `lint-fish`, `lint-markdown`,
`lint-json`, then `make test-ci`. Missing: `lint-md-tables`,
`lint-editorconfig`.

`make test-ci` (Makefile:197) only bootstraps fisher and installs the plugin —
it asserts nothing about behavior.

13 unit test files (`tests/unit/*.fish`) and 1 integration test
(`tests/integration/test_version_switching.fish`) exist and are executed by no
workflow. `.claude/rules/lint-before-commit.md` mandates `make lint` and
`make test-unit` before every commit; CI enforces neither.

## Impact

A commit that breaks Markdown table alignment, EditorConfig compliance, or any
of the 14 tests passes CI green. The only enforcement of those rules is a local
convention document.

## Fix

In `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, replace the three individual lint steps with a
single `make lint`, and add test steps:

      - name: Lint
        run: make lint

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: make test-unit

      - name: Run integration tests
        run: make test-integration

      - name: Test plugin installation
        run: make test-ci

## Resolution
lint.yml: three individual lint steps replaced with 'make lint'; added 'make test-unit' and 'make test-integration' steps. Verified locally: make lint exit=0, test-unit exit=0, test-integration exit=0.
title: CI runs 3 of 5 lint targets and none of the test suite

body:
## Problem

Class: excess-permissions. A write scope the job provably does not use.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/stale.yml:22`:

    contents: write # only for delete-branch option

The job's single step is
`ivuorinen/actions/stale@de31e11dda6488eabe95e951ebb61c6d9d500865`. That
composite action's `action.yml` at that exact SHA declares only three inputs —
`token`, `days-before-stale`, `days-before-close` — and its `actions/stale@v10.3.0`
step never sets `delete-branch`. `actions/stale` defaults `delete-branch` to
`false`. The comment justifies a feature the pinned action cannot reach.

The action's own documented permission block (comments in its `action.yml`)
lists only `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write`.

## Impact

A daily scheduled run on a public repository holds a `contents: write`
GITHUB_TOKEN. If the third-party action is compromised at a future SHA bump,
the blast radius includes writing repository contents rather than being limited
to issue and PR metadata.

## Fix

Delete line 22 of `.github/workflows/stale.yml`. The job keeps
`issues: write` and `pull-requests: write`, which the action does use.

## Resolution
stale.yml: removed 'contents: write'. Job retains issues:write and pull-requests:write, the only scopes the pinned action uses.
title: stale.yml grants unused contents write scope

body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:8` declares a bare `push:` with no `branches:`
filter, so every push to every branch starts a `LintPush` run — in addition to
the `LintPR` run the same push triggers via `pull_request`. The two runs use
different `github.ref` values (`refs/heads/<branch>` vs `refs/pull/N/merge`), so
the `concurrency` group does not deduplicate them.

## Evidence

For a single renovate push on 2026-08-03:

    30777396138  pull_request  PR Lint  renovate/actions-setup-node-6.x  3m15s
    30777395855  push          PR Lint  renovate/actions-setup-node-6.x  3m16s

Both ran the full MegaLinter suite (grype 58s, checkov 18s, trivy 11s). The
`push` run also duplicates `lint.yml`'s push trigger on `main`.

## Impact

Every push costs roughly double the runner time, and PR status lists carry two
identical checks, making the "which one gates?" question in the
non-gating-check finding harder to answer.

## Fix

Scope the push trigger to the default branch in
`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml`:

    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      pull_request:
        branches: [main]

## Resolution
pr-lint.yml: push trigger scoped to 'branches: [main]'.
title: Unfiltered push trigger double-runs MegaLinter on every PR branch

body:
## Problem

The two lint workflows gate on different, partly non-existent branch sets.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/lint.yml:9,11` — `branches: [main, develop]`
`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:10` — `branches: [master, main]`

`git ls-remote --heads origin` lists only `main`, `chore/upgrades`, and three
`renovate/*` branches. Neither `develop` nor `master` exists. The repository's
default branch is `main`.

## Impact

Dead configuration that silently misroutes if either name is ever created: a
`develop` branch would get `Lint` but not `PR Lint`; a `master` branch would get
`PR Lint` but not `Lint`. Reviewers reading either file get a wrong picture of
the branching model.

## Fix

Set both workflows to `branches: [main]` in every trigger.

## Resolution
lint.yml and pr-lint.yml triggers both set to 'branches: [main]'; removed non-existent develop and master.
title: Workflow branch filters name branches that do not exist and disagree

body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/stale.yml:10` declares `workflow_call:`, publishing the
workflow as a reusable workflow. No workflow in this repository calls it, and
the repository is public, so any workflow the owner controls elsewhere can
invoke it — inheriting the job's `contents: write`, `issues: write`, and
`pull-requests: write` scopes against this repository.

## Evidence

`grep -r "uses:.*stale.yml" .github/` returns nothing; the only invocations
observed in `gh run list` are `schedule` events.

## Impact

Unused trigger surface on a write-capable job. A `workflow_call` entry point is
not gated by the `pull_request` review rule and is easy to overlook when
auditing what can mutate issues and PRs.

## Fix

Delete line 10 (`workflow_call:`) from `.github/workflows/stale.yml`. The
`schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers cover the workflow's actual use.
Re-add it only when a caller exists.

## Resolution
stale.yml: removed the unused workflow_call trigger; schedule and workflow_dispatch retained.
title: stale.yml exposes an unused workflow_call trigger with write scopes

body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/lint.yml:30-31` runs `actions/setup-node` with no
`node-version` or `node-version-file`, so the step is a no-op that leaves the
runner-image default Node in place.

## Evidence

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e # v6.4.0

No `with:` block. The linters it feeds are `npx --yes markdownlint-cli@<pinned>`
and friends from the `Makefile`; the tool versions are pinned but the Node major
executing them is not.

## Impact

An `ubuntu-latest` image bump changes the Node major without a commit to this
repository. `npx` resolution and linter behavior can shift underneath pinned
tool versions. Advisory: no current failure, and the repository has no root
`.nvmrc` to derive a version from.

## Fix

Pin the major explicitly:

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e # v6.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

## Resolution
lint.yml: setup-node pinned to node-version '24' (current Active LTS) rather than the '22' the finding drafted.
title: setup-node pins no Node version

body:
## Resolution
`make lint-fix` ran `markdown-table-formatter` against `.claude/rules/*.md`
  and `README.md`. The formatter outputs "No markdown table formatting has been
  applied." to stdout (and exits 0) on files with no Markdown tables, causing
  the Makefile's `<"$file" >"$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$file"` pattern to overwrite
  all six files with that single-line message.
  Fixed by: (1) restoring all six files from their last clean git commit via
  `git show <sha>:<path>`; (2) adding `-not -path './.claude/rules/*'` to the
  `lint-md-tables` and `lint-fix` table-formatter loops in `Makefile` so these
  files are excluded in all future runs.

Migrated from v1 `doc-findings.md` (Pass 1, 2026-05-08).

body:
## Resolution
The `lint-fix` target used `<"$file" >"$tmp"` stdin/stdout redirection — wrong for `markdown-table-formatter`, which takes file arguments and modifies in-place. When stdout was not the file content, the formatter emitted "No markdown table formatting has been applied." (a diagnostic message, not file content), which overwrote every processed file with that 47-byte string. Fixed by: (1) restoring all six corrupted files from git; (2) rewriting `lint-md-tables` and `lint-fix` table-formatter steps to pass files as positional arguments; (3) adding `-not -path './.claude/rules/*'` exclusion to both targets.

Migrated from v1 `nitpicker-findings.md` (Pass 2, 2026-05-14).

body:
## Problem

The directory walk uses `dirname` to move up the tree. A circular symlink could theoretically cause an infinite loop.

## Evidence

Walk terminates on `/`; `dirname` operates on path strings not filesystem traversal, so circular symlinks cannot cause infinite loops.

## Impact

Extremely unlikely; no practical risk.

## Fix

No action required.

## Resolution
Disproven by the finding's own Evidence and confirmed against functions/nvm_find_nvmrc.fish:39. The walk does 'set dir (dirname "$dir")' — pure string manipulation, never a filesystem traversal — and breaks unconditionally at 'if test "$dir" = /' (line 36). No symlink is ever followed, so a circular symlink cannot produce an infinite loop. The record carried Fix: 'No action required' while status stayed open, so INDEX.md reported a false unresolved finding.
title: `nvm_find_nvmrc` traversal has no guard against circular symlinks

body:
## Problem

`_nvm_cache_stats` and three sites in `nvm_doctor` probe for `fd` with
`command -q fd` and, on success, trust its output. A version-manager shim
(mise, asdf) satisfies `command -q` because the shim binary is on PATH, but
running it can fail — printing an error to stderr and nothing to stdout. The
count then reads as 0 with no indication anything went wrong.

## Evidence

`functions/nvm_cache.fish:101-105`:

    if command -q fd
        echo "Cache files: "(count (fd --type f . "$cache_dir" 2>/dev/null))
    else
        echo "Cache files: "(count (find "$cache_dir" -type f 2>/dev/null))
    end

Reproduced on a host where `fd` is a mise shim with no version selected
(exercised accidentally while isolating XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the test harness):

    $ fd --type f . "$cache_dir"
    mise ERROR No version is set for shim: fd
    $ echo $status
    0-output, no stdout

With two files present in the cache directory:

    fd count   = 0
    find count = 2
    du -sh     = 12K

`nvm_cache stats` reported `Cache files: 0` alongside `Cache size: 12K` — two
lines of the same output contradicting each other.

The `2>/dev/null` on the `fd` call suppresses the shim's error, so nothing
surfaces to the user.

## Impact

`nvm_cache stats` and `nvm_doctor` report an empty cache on any host where
`fd` is an unresolved shim. `nvm_doctor` is the command users run when
something is already wrong; it hands them a false "cache is empty" reading and
sends them down the wrong path. Same pattern at `nvm_doctor.fish:207`, `:299`,
`:349`.

## Fix

Do not treat `command -q` as proof the tool works. Capture the result and fall
back when it is empty:

    set -l files
    if command -q fd
        set files (fd --type f . "$cache_dir" 2>/dev/null)
    end
    if test (count $files) -eq 0
        set files (find "$cache_dir" -type f 2>/dev/null)
    end
    echo "Cache files: "(count $files)

Apply the same shape to the three `nvm_doctor` sites. Alternatively drop `fd`
entirely — `find` is already the fallback, is always present, and this is not
a hot path.

## Resolution
Removed fd from all four sites (nvm_cache.fish:101, nvm_doctor.fish:307/323/357) rather than hardening the probe — every fd branch already had an exactly-equivalent find fallback directly below it, so the fix is a pure deletion onto an already-exercised path. Net -23 lines of production code, no new branches. Regression test added: tests/unit/test_cache.fish::test_cache_stats_with_broken_fd puts a stub fd on PATH that exits 1 with no stdout, mimicking an unresolved mise shim, and asserts the count is still correct. Mutation-verified: passes on the fix, fails when the fd branch is reintroduced.
title: command -q fd accepts a broken shim, silently reporting zero files

body:
## Problem

Class: non-gating-check. Verified.

`Lint` and `PR Lint` both trigger on `pull_request` and run linters/validators, so
both are gate candidates. The repository's only ruleset (`main`, id 4676324,
enforcement `active`) contains no `required_status_checks` rule, and classic
branch protection is absent. Nothing blocks a merge on a red check.

## Evidence

`gh api repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/rulesets/4676324` rule types:
`deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `creation`, `required_linear_history`,
`pull_request`, `copilot_code_review`. No `required_status_checks`.

`gh api repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/branches/main/protection`
-> 404 "Branch not protected".

Consequence already observed: `PR Lint` concluded `failure` on every open
renovate PR since 2026-08-03 (runs 30777396138, 30777392536) and those PRs
remained mergeable. A genuinely broken `editorconfig-checker` installer also
sat on `main` undetected, because no required check exercised it.

Check-run names confirmed against PR #10 head
(`gh api repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/commits/<sha>/check-runs`):
`Lint codebase` (success), `Lint on pull request` (success),
`Lint on push` (skipped).

## Impact

Any PR can be merged into `main` with lint and workflow-security checks red.
The `pull_request` review rule requires 1 approval but approval does not read
check status, so a broken change merges on a rubber-stamp review.

## Fix

Add a `required_status_checks` rule to ruleset 4676324 with the two
pull-request check-run names as contexts. Never auto-applied — the user runs
it.

`PUT` replaces the **entire** ruleset and rejects the server-managed fields the
`GET` returns, so the field-stripping and the rule update must both actually
execute. Requires `jq` (installed by `make install-tools`). The commands below
avoid shell-specific control flow so they work in `fish`, `bash`, and `sh`
alike.

Step 1 — fetch, strip server-managed fields, set the rule:

    gh api repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/rulesets/4676324 > /tmp/rs.json

    jq 'del(._links, .created_at, .updated_at, .id, .node_id,
            .source, .source_type, .current_user_can_bypass)
        | .rules = ((.rules | map(select(.type != "required_status_checks")))
          + [{
              "type": "required_status_checks",
              "parameters": {
                "strict_required_status_checks_policy": true,
                "do_not_enforce_on_create": false,
                "required_status_checks": [
                  {"context": "Lint codebase"},
                  {"context": "Lint on pull request"}
                ]
              }
            }])' /tmp/rs.json > /tmp/rs-updated.json

`.rules =` with the type filtered out replaces any existing
`required_status_checks` rule rather than appending, so re-running the
procedure is idempotent and cannot accumulate duplicate rules.

Step 2 — confirm nothing changed server-side since Step 1, then `PUT`:

    gh api repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/rulesets/4676324 > /tmp/rs-recheck.json
    jq -S . /tmp/rs.json         > /tmp/rs-a.json
    jq -S . /tmp/rs-recheck.json > /tmp/rs-b.json
    diff /tmp/rs-a.json /tmp/rs-b.json

If `diff` prints anything, the ruleset was edited between Step 1 and now —
discard everything and start again from Step 1. Only when `diff` is silent:

    gh api -X PUT repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/rulesets/4676324 \
      --input /tmp/rs-updated.json

This narrows the read-modify-write window; it does not close it. GitHub
documents no `If-Match`/conditional-update support for this endpoint, so a
concurrent edit landing between the `diff` and the `PUT` would still be
overwritten. Run it when no one else is editing repository rulesets.

Step 3 — verify the contexts landed, not merely that the rule type exists. A
`required_status_checks` rule with an empty array gates nothing:

    gh api repos/ivuorinen/nvm-auto-use.fish/rulesets/4676324 \
      --jq '.rules[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks")
            | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context'

Expected output, exactly these two lines:

    Lint codebase
    Lint on pull request

`Lint on push` is deliberately excluded, but not because it would block
merges. Its job-level `if: github.event_name == 'push'`
(`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:20`) skips it on `pull_request` events, and a
job skipped by a job-level condition reports `Success` — confirmed on PR #10's
head, where the `Lint on push` check-run carried conclusion `skipped`, not
pending. Requiring it would therefore add a permanently green check that
validates no pull-request linting at all.

The pending-check trap that does block merges applies to workflow-level
skips — `paths`, `paths-ignore`, `branches`, or `branches-ignore` filters that
stop the workflow from starting, so no check-run is ever created.
`pr-lint.yml` triggers on both `push` and `pull_request`, so its workflow
always runs on a PR and both jobs always report.

## Resolution
Applied to ruleset 4676324 on 2026-08-11 using the procedure documented in this finding, run verbatim. Step 2's re-fetch/diff gate was silent, so the PUT proceeded. Verified after: required_status_checks contexts are exactly 'Lint codebase' and 'Lint on pull request'; exactly one required_status_checks rule (no duplicate from the idempotent jq); enforcement active; strict_required_status_checks_policy true. Diffing the pre-change backup against the result with the new rule filtered out is byte-identical, so no pre-existing rule was altered. Backup of the prior ruleset retained out-of-tree.
title: Gate-shaped workflows are not required status checks
